CONTEXT I AM EXPLICITLY NOT CHARGING TO THIS PR.

C1. MERGE COMMITS ARE INVISIBLE TO THE LANE GATE, INCLUDING CONFLICT RESOLUTIONS. lwb_lanes.commit_files runs `git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r --root <sha>`, which prints NOTHING for a merge commit. This branch's a3be81c3 is 'Merge origin/main ..., resolve HANDOFF.md conflict'; `git diff-tree --cc a3be81c3` shows HANDOFF.md as content unique to the merge, while commit_files returns []. With no files, touches_shared stays false, so neither lane classification nor the shared-path review requirement applies to a hand-resolved conflict in the file CLAUDE.md orders every session to read first. Pre-existing on main and untouched by this diff, so not charged -- but it is a live hole and this PR happens to exercise it.

C2. proof/39.json MARKS A STATE-DEPENDENT COMMAND `verifiable: true`, AND IT NOW MISMATCHES. `python scripts/lwb_check_proof.py --reexecute` on this branch:
    FAIL python3 scripts/lwb_handoff.py --check (sha256 0d77aee8... != recorded ab8f5e3b...)
    TOTAL: 27 of 152 commands re-executed, 0 uncomparable, 18 skipped-self, across 22 records -- MISMATCH: 1   EXIT 1
The cause is not a sanitiser gap -- the repo path IS sanitised to `<repo>/`. It is the byte count: proof/39.json recorded 'OK: <repo>/HANDOFF.md passes all checks (2961 bytes)' and this branch's HANDOFF.md is 2995 bytes. proof/README.md states the rule verbatim -- a command is verifiable:true ONLY if its output cannot vary at ANY later commit, and explicitly names 'a byte count' as disqualifying. proof/39.json breaks its own README's rule, and the consequence is that EVERY future PR touching HANDOFF.md will report this mismatch. It is report-only today; proof/README.md anticipates a later PR making it blocking, at which point main is already red. Entirely main's, not this PR's -- I raise it because this PR is the first thing to surface it and the next HANDOFF.md edit will hit it too.
